name: South Gate City Council/ South Gate Housing Authority/ Successor Agency to the Community Development Commission of the City of South Gate
minutes_text:
CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE

  SOUTH  GATE  CITY  COUNCIL;  SOUTH  GATE  HOUSING  AUTHORITY;
  SUCCESSOR  AGENCY  TO THE  COMMUNITY  DEVELOPMENT
COMMISSION  OF THE  CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE;  SOUTH  GATE  UTILITY
  AUTHORITY;  AND  SOUTH  GATE  PUBLIC  FINANCE  AUTHORITY

  REGULAR  MEETING  MINUTES

  TUESDAY,  JULY  22, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  The Regular  meeting  of the City  Council,  Housing  Authority,  Successor
  Agency,  was called  to order by Maria  Davila,  Mayor/Chairperson  at 6:36
  p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina De La Rosa, Deputy  Director  of Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OF

ALLEGIANCE  Thurman  Green,  Risk Manager

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk/Recording  Secretary

PRESENT  Mayor/Chairperson  Maria  Davila,  Vice Mayor/Vice  Chairperson  Joshua
  Barron,  Council/Authority/Agency  Member  Gil Hurtado,
  Council/Authority/Agency  Member  Al Rios, City  Treasurer  Jose De La
  Paz, City  Manager/Executive  Director  Rob Houston,  City Attorney/
  Authority  Counsel  Raul F. Salinas

  Council  Member  Maria  del Pilar Avalos  requested  that she be allowed  to
  participate  in the City  Council  Meeting  remotely  due to medical  condition
  and consistent  with  AB  2449. The request  was approved  by motion  of
  Council  Member  Hurtado  and seconded  by Mayor  Davila.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Hurtado,  yes; Council  Member  Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,  yes.

l

BUDGET  ADMIN  The City  Council:

  a.  Received  and filed  presentations  on the Proposed  FY 2025-26  Budgets
  and 1-Year  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP");

  b.  Adopted  Resolution  No. 2025-23-CC  entitled  A Joint  Resolution  of the
  City  Council  of the City  of South  Gate, South  Gate Housing  Authority
  and Successor  Agency  to the Community  Development  Commission
  of the City  of South  Gate, California,  approving  the FY 2025-26
  Municipal  Budget  in the amount  of $298,586,637, including  all funds
  and departments,  along  with  any additions  or deletions  the Legislative
  Bodies  may enact; and
   REGULAR  COUNCIL,  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  & SUCCESSOR  AGENCY
  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JTJLY  22, 2025

l
BUDGET  ADMnV

CONT'D  c.  Adopted  Resolution  No. 2025-24-CC  entitled  Resolution  of the City
  Council  of the City  of South Gate, California,  establishing  the FY
  2025-26  Gann Appropriations  Limit  in the amount  of $110,869,454.

  City  Manager  Houston  stated tonight's  public  hearing  and presentation  of
  the budget  for the coming  fiscal  year. There  was a presentation  given  at
  the first  meeting  in June which  highlighted  the core pieces of the budget,
  operations  and accomplishments  from  last year.

  City  Manager  Houston  asked Mr. Frausto,  Director  of Administrative
  Services,  to start the presentation.

  Mr. Frausto  presented  the Fiscal  Year 2025/26  Proposed  Budget  for
  adoption.  Mr. Frausto  deferred  to a couple  of department  heads to speak
  about some of the growth  and costs the city has experienced  over the last
  several  years.

  Chief  of Police  Arakawa  gave his presentation.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  gave his presentation.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works,  gave his presentation.

  Mr. Houston  spoke on the options  the city is facing,  details  on those
  options  and a recommendation  approach  for this yeais  budget.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  explained  that freezing  positions  are also
  freezing  services.  He met with  the directors  and discussed  their budgets.

RECESS  Prior  to the conclusion  of item 1, the City  Council  recessed  at 7:53 p.m.,
  and reconvened  at 7:59 p.m.,  with  all Members  of Council  present.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if anyone  in the audience  wished  to speak on this
  item.

  Sylvia  Lopez,  San Luis Ave.,  is representing  her local  swim  team,  South
  Gate Aqua  Coalition.  Her team practices  at the Patricia  Mitchell  Swim
  Stadium  and is concerned  that the swimming  stadium  will  be closed  from
  November  to January.

  Jayla Bonilla,  3220 Liberty  Ave.,  is a member  of the South  Gate Aqua
  Coalition  and is concerned  that the swimming  stadium  will  be closed  from
  November  to January.

BUDGETADMIN

CONT'D  Yolanda  Macias  has been part of the aquatics  since 1971 and does not
  mind  paying  a few dollars  more so the swimming  stadium  can remain
  open.

  Freda,  nine-years-old,  was diagnosed  with ADHD.  She has a lot of energy
  and swimming  has kept her focused.

  Pedro  Espejo  is a member  of the South  Gate Aqua  Coalition  and is
  concerned  that the swimming  stadium  will  be closed  for three months.

  Liz Ruiz,  Parks Commissioner,  listening  to the swim  participants  voicing

  their  concern  warms  her heart.  She is also concerned  about the budget  cuts
  and supports  the second proposal  that does not include  the closure  of the
  pool.  She thinks  the Utility  Users Tax is something  the residents  should
  consider  as a city.  She also believes  that there has not been enough
  outreach  for these meetings.

  Francisco  Gallegos,  Otis st., is concerned  about public  safety and the cuts
  that are going  to possibly  happen.

  Erika  Diaz,  parent  of a South  Gate swimmer.  She is expressing  her strong
  support  for keeping  the South  Gate pool open.

  Gavin  Padilla  is present  supporting  his swimming  team in hopes of
  keeping  the swimming  pool open in December,  January,  and February.

  Karen  is expressing  her support  for keeping  the South  Gate pool  open. Her
  son is autistic,  and swimming  has helped  him to deal with  life.

  Mariah  Tavaris  is new to the South  Gate team.  She is a JAG and SAG
  qualifier  and is expressing  her support  for keeping  the South Gate pool
  open.

  Jr Bonilla  has been swimming  for the South  Gate Aqua  Coalition  for four
  years.  He is expressing  his support  for keeping  the South  Gate pool  open.

  Jirnmy  Ozaeta,  South  Gate resident,  is requesting  that the City  Council
  lead with  transparency  and respect  for our civil  responsibilities.  For the
  past several  Council  Meetings,  several  questions  have been posed by city
  residents  regarding  the city budget.  These questions  have not been
  answered  by the City  Council  or staff.

  Nelson  Hermosillo,  1035 Dorothy  Ave.,  commended  Mr. Houston  for the
  presentation.  He recommends  option  two.  He asked if the city becomes
  insolvent,  what  happens  to the retirees  and their  pensions.  He has analyzed

l
BUDGET  ADMIN

CONT'D  the budget  for the State of California,  the County  of Los Angeles,  and the
  City  of South  Gate's.  The state and county  are spending  money  unwisely.
  He has called  assemblymen,  senators,  and county  supervisors  without  any
  luck.

  Edgar  Pelayo,  South  Gate resident,  informed  the South  Gate Aquatic
  Center  that every  second  Thursday  of the month,  there's  a Parks & Rec
  Commission  meeting.  He doesn't  think  asking  South  Gate residents  to tax
  themselves  will  be a solution  to the situation  the city is in. He mentioned
  that this city government  is financed  by the residents.  Changes  need to be
  made.

  Juan, South  Gate resident,  after seeing the presentation,  believes  changes
  are necessary.

  Having  no one else come forward,  Mayor  Davila  closed  the audience
  portion.

  Mayor  Davila  thanked  the South  Gate Aquatic  team for attending  tonight's
  meeting  and speaking  on the swimming  pool  closure.  She doesn't  agree
  with  option  one, option  two is more helpful.

  Mayor  Davila  asked why  parks are asking  to close on Fridays.

  Mr. Costley  stated Fridays  are the least used day at the pool.  Lessons  are
  held on Monday  through  Thursday  on a regular  basis. The parks recently
  within  the last couple  of years reopened  Fridays.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated that it is easy to critique  and not give any
  solutions.  He mentioned  that the employees  are not highly  paid. This is a
  hard blue color,  hardworking  community.  We have had structural  deficits
  throughout  the year. The streetlight  and landscaping  fund was mentioned
  during  the presentation  which  everyone  in the community  benefits  from.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  thanked  all the young  people  present  tonight
  who spoke.  He has a grandson  that's  also on the spectrum  and he's into
  music.  If it wasn't  for the music  his grandson  wouldn't  be as advanced  as
  he is. He appreciates  the parents  who came here with  her son. He
  understands  the seniors  need the swimming  pool for their therapy.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  is not going  to support  closing  the swimming
  pool,  removing  crossing  guards,  and freezing  programs  long term.  The
  city is going  to tell voters,  here's your  choice,  you can either  support  this
  tax that every  city around  us has. City  employees  are leaving  for better
  paid jobs.  Council  Member  Hurtado  was out there with  the teachers  at

  Page 4 of 15
   REGULAR  COUNCIL,  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  & SUCCESSOR  AGENCY
  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JULY  22, 2025

1
BUDGET  AJ)MnV

CONT'D  UTLA  when they were marching  for better  salaries.  He out there with  the
  Kaiser  nurses and first responders  for the same thing  at St. Francis.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  the people  for attending  tonight's  meeting.
  He asked Mr. Costley  the reason behind  closing  the pool  on Fridays  if the
  budget  hasn't  been approved.

  Mr. Costley  stated as we move  forward  in this program  and we set goals of
  how we were going  to set the budget,  the recommendation  from  staff was
  for option  number  two.  Staff originally  expected  the budget  to be
  approved  at the end of June and not in July, we could  not meet those
  budget  numbers  if we did not close the pool.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  Mr. Costley  for clarifying.  He responded  to
  some of his colleagues'  comments  regarding  his Parks & Recreation
  Commissioner  and Planning  Commissioner  who happened  to be very
  involved.  This is a democracy  where  people  question,  especially  the city
  budget.

  Council  Member  Rios asked Mr. Costley  if the city's  water  is free or do
  the departments  also pay for the water.

  Mr. Costley  will  have Mr. Frausto  or Mr. Cervantes  answer  the question.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated the city has its own water  district.  The City  of South
  Gate should  be paying  into the water  enterprise.  He doesn't  know  when  it
  was shifted  because  the city is using  water  for the city's  pool  and medians.

  Mr. Houston  stated for water  services,  water  staffing,  and water  costs are
  not funded  out of the general  fund.  Water  is considered  a special  :[und, and
  it pays for itself  because  the rates keep getting  adjusted  as costs go up.

  Council  Member  Rios stated that questions  asked by the public  are
  answered  but some questions  have not been answered,  for example  the
  UUT  survey  that was conducted.

  Council  MemberAvalos  stated that she will  not burden  the city's  deficit
  solely  on the residents.  She is suggesting  the city conduct  a full budget
  audit with  the goal of identifying  inefficiencies,  outdated  contracts,  unused
  assets, and overlapping  services.  Evaluating  consultant  contracts,  travel
  expenses,  and administrative  overhead.  Freezing  non-essential  hiring  and
  overtime.  Implementing  a temporary  hiring  freeze  for non-critical
  positions.  Review  overtime  usage in all departments.  Reassigning  staff
  where  possible  before  adding  new roles.  Renegotiating  vendor  contracts
  and service  agreements.  Streamlining  all the departments,  combining

  Page 5 of 15
   REGULAR  COUNCIL,  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  &  SUCCESSOR  AGENCY
  MEETING  MINUTES  OF  JULY  22, 2025

1
B[mGETADMIN

CONT'D  departments  that overlap  responsibilities.  Cross  training  the employees  to

  increase  flexibility  and reduce  overtime  dependency.

  Council  Member  Avalos  also recommends  launching  a Community
  Budget  Advisory  Task Force,  involving  the residents  in budget
  prioritization,  promoting  transparency,  a public  buying  when  difficult

  choices  need to be made  because  that  is coming  in the next  fiscal  year.

  Introducing  a target  fee adjustment,  revisiting  outdated  or underpriced  user

  fees such  as in the city's  rental  facilities,  permits,  or special  programs,  and

  making  sure these  increases  are minimal  and tied  to the service  delivery  of

  our residents.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  thanked  the South  Gate Aquatics  Team  for attending

  tonight's  meeting.  He knows  the impact  sports  have  on one's  life.  He
  understands  no one wants  to pay more  taxes.  He mentioned  the street  and

  landscaping  funds  have  not been raised  in 30 years.  How  can residents
  help.

  Council  Member  Rios  stated  that the City  Council  created  an Ad Hoc
  Committee  to see the city's  budget.  The Ad  Hock  Committee  received
  information,  and they  also asked  for certain  information  that was not
  provided.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  stated  that  after  reviewing  the proposed
  budget,  he commends  staff  for the work  done  to control  expenses  under  a

  very  challenging  financial  situation.  Meaningful  efforts  have  been made  to

  reduce  costs,  but we all know  prices  continue  to rise whether  it's

  insurance,  food,  school  supplies  and there's  only  so much  any individual
  could  do to cut before  the impact  can be felt.  The  city  is facing  a revenue

  challenge.  Discussion  will  take time,  and the community  should  be
  involved  in shaping  that future.  He suggested  traffic  mitigation,  curb  usage

  fee, vacant  property  or empty  storefront  tax. He recommends  that the City
  Council  adopt  the proposed  FY 2025/26  budget  with  option  two  cutting

  2.2 million  and leaving  the pool  intact  with  its original  operating  hours.  He

  is requesting  that  city  staff  conduct  a quarterly  update  to be provided  to

  City  Council  and residents  on all cost-saving  measures  that are being
  approved  today  and all proposed  cuts.

  Mr.  Houston  stated  good  discussion,  good  community  input,  tough  road

  ahead.  It will  take the entire  community,  staff  and council.  Option  two
  could  reduce  touch  decisions  and give  us time  over  this next  year. He

  commended  the finance  department  for their  hard  work.

  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JULY  22, 2025

l
BUDGET  ADMIN

CONT'D  Mr. Houston  stated he is available  to go through  the budget  in detail  with
  members  of the community,  set up a workshop  or a cornrnunity  meeting.
  He will  have Chief  Arakawa  speak on the horses.

  Chief  Arakawa  explained  that there is no line item on the budget  for
  horses because  the Police  Offices  Association  had an idea of having  a
  mounted  patrol  unit with  the horses and trailers  owned  by the police
  officers,  housed  by the police  officers  at their residences,  insurance  and
  everything  else associated  with  that program  paid by the police  officers.
  No taxpayers'  dollars  are being  used for the mounted  unit. Two horses
  wouldn't  be the cause of a deficit  to this degree.

  Mayor  Davila  inquired  about the Azalea  Festival  and lack of participation.
  She asked if the Tweedy  Mile  runs the car show what  does the city
  provides.

  Mr. Costley  stated the city provides  some police  services,  show mobile
  staffing  for the event and overtime  fees across the board.  Use of the golf
  course  the whole  day. Staff meet with  the Tweedy  Mile  on a regular  basis
  to get the event moving  forward.

  Mayor  Davila  is suggesting  that Tweedy  Mile  pay for their  event.

  Mr. Costley  informed  City  Council  that the Tweedy  Mile  do not make a
  significant  amount  of profit  to pay for their event.

  Mayor  Davila  believes  the city can do without  the carnival  during  the
  fourth  of July event.

  Mr. Costley  informed  City  Council  that the carnival  is the moneymaker  for
  both Azalea  and fourth  of July events.  For the Azalea  festival  we bring  in
  about $15,000  to $18,000 a year. For the fourth  of July we bring in about
  $18,000.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  questioned  the expenses  from  both events.

  Mr. Frausto  stated these costs are our best estimates.  The Public  Works
  and Police  Departments  do contribute  to the setup and success of these
  events that are not factored  in here. He does not have a tangible  dollar,
  that's  why  it was not included.

  Mayor  Davila  questioned  the $60,000  for one day on the swimming
  stadium.

  Page 7 of 15
   REGULAR  COUNCIL,  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  & SUCCESSOR  AGENCY
  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JULY  22, 2025

l
BUDGET  ADMIN

CONT'D  Mr. Costley  stated that it is one day per week.  So, 52 weeks  a year. A
  swimming  stadium  takes significant  staffing  to match  crowds.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if other 'tunding  could  be used for the swimming
  stadium.

  Mr. Costley  stated that there might  be funding,  but it is not in the Parks
  and Recreation  Department.

  Mr. Houston  stated City  Council  can provide  guidance  and staff will  find  a
  solution.

  Council  Member  Rios inquired  about UWS.

  Mr. Houston  stated the city has a UWS  fiind  of $120,000  per year as part
  of the trash contract  where  they contribute  to community  events.  However,
  that fund is being  utilized  for Winter  Wonderland,  and other evems as
  well.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  recommends  going  with  option  two. Don't
  touch  the swimming  stadium,  golf  course,  or free play. Eliminate  the other
  two but bring  them back later to see maybe  we can find  a way to fund
  those.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  has met with  city  staff and people  in the
  community  to get a sense of what people  want.  People  want more services,
  not less.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  motioned  for the second  option,  keeping  the
  swimming  stadium,  golf  course,  and free play  intact,  and return  by
  November  with  some ideas for the other two options  and seconded  by
  Vice  Mayor  Barron.

  Council  MemberAvalos  needs clarification  that at the first presentation
  Mr. Downs  indicated  that the budget  already  included  salary increases  for
  our employees.

  Mr. Houston  stated the cola, which  has typically  been offered  over the
  years for cost-of-living  increase,  which  equates  to 3%, has been
  anticipated  and put in the budget  as a forecasted  cost just  like costs for
  potential  projects  or even staffing  levels.  However,  there is no connection
  with  the funding  that put in that budget  to actual  guarantees  to spend it.
  So, there's  a separate process  that runs parallel  to the budget  that is labor
  negotiations.  That number  will  be based on negotiations  with  the unions
  and city council.

BUDGET  ADMm

CONT'D  Council  Member  Rios is asking  for an amendment  on the motion  to
  include  quarterly.  He would  like the Ad Hoc Committee  to continue
  meeting  with  staff to discuss  budget.

  Mayor  Davila  agrees that staff will  provide  a quarterly  budget  report  for
  the City  Council and Ad Hoc Committee  and City  Treasurer  will  continue
  meeting  with staff.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  stated that there is a misconception  that City  Council
  only hears information  if an Ad Hoc Committee  was created.  If he has any
  questions,  he contacts  the finance  director  or any other director  and with
  city manager  too.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council/Authority/Agency  Member  Hurtado,  yes;
  Council/Authority/Agency  Member  Rios,  yes; Vice Mayor/Vice
  Chairperson  Barron,  yes; Mayor/Chairperson  Davila,  yes;
  Council/Authority/Agency  Member  Avalos,  no.

RECESS  The City  Council  recessed  at 9:54 p.m., and reconvened  at 9:59 p.m., with
  all Members  of Council  present.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  - NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  Nelson  Hermosillo,  10135  Dorothy  Ave., thanked  Council  Member  Rios
  for his comments  on the budget.  He couldn't  attend the previous  meeting
  regarding  CDBG  funds.  He praises  the public  works  department.  He stated
  that although  it was a great gesture  to use CDBG  funds to supply  food to
  the immigrant  community,  the city cannot  afford  this. He is requesting  that
  the streets and sidewalks  be fixed.  He also mentioned  that if the Trump
  Administration  is aware,  the federal  funds  will  be taken from  the city.

  Mr. Hermosillo  agrees the city employees  are underpaid  and that's  why
  they are leaving  for other cities.  He is suggesting  reducing  the department
  heads'  salaries.

  Mayor  Davila  stated the city  is aware  federal  funds  cannot  be used to
  supply  food to the immigrant  community.

  Francisco  Gallegos,  Otis Street,  spoke on the issue of Fireworks.

  Liz Ruiz,  Kauffman  Ave.,  cornrnended  the city  for their work  reminding
  the people  that we share the streets with  bike riders.  She asked about the
  hazard  mitigation  plan. And  who to call regarding  the removal  of certain
  trees.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Chief  Arakawa  stated  that the Police  Department  was responsible  for the

  hazard  mitigation  plan,  which  is done  every  five  years.  It is a requirement
  for CalOES  and FEMA  to ensure  the cities  have  a plan  in case of a nature
  disaster.

  Chief  Arakawa  provided  a letter  to City  Manager  and City  Council
  regarding  his retirement  from  the South  Gate  Police  Department  effective
  Thursday,  October  16, 2025.  He has served  for 33 years.  Serving  as Police

  Chief  has been one of the greatest  honors  of his professional  career  and is

  forever  grateful  for the trust  and support  given  to him  by the City  Council,

  this  wonderful  community,  the Police  Department,  and City  Manager.

  Mayor  Davila  is thankful  for having  Darren  Arakawa  as Police  Chief.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated  that  on behalf  of his family  and himself

  they  are grateful  for the work  the Police  Department  has done  for this
  community.

  Council  Member  Rios  is thankful  for having  Darren  Arakawa  as Police
  Chief.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  thanked  Chief  Arakawa  for everything  he has done  for

  this  community.

  Council  Member  Avalos  is sorry  to hear  Chief  Arakawa  is retiring  but

  understands  in life  tough  decisions  must  be made.  She is thankful  for

  everything  he has done  for this  community.

  Rail  F. Salinas,  City  Attorney  stated  that  it is a bittersweet  moment  and

  loss to the City  of South  Gate.  He stated  the city  owes  Chief  Arakawa  a

  debt  of gratitude  for everything  he has done  for this  community.

  Mayor  Davila  would  like  to see a presentation  by ChiefArakawa  from  his

  first  day of work  to the end.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works,  there  were  questions  with

  regards  to the maintenance  of our city  trees  and where  we are removing
  trees  and being  grateful  that some  trees were  removed.  A couple  of years
  ago, the city  did a survey.  It was kind  of a hazardous  mitigation  type

  survey  where  all the 18,000  city  trees  were  looked  at their  condition.  We

  developed  three  phases  of removal,  and all trees have been  removed.  If a
